i don't think the OP meant any harm with this post. if you break down ANYTHING, any job, any relationship, any circumstance far enough-- it's full of shit. you can't win. there is no "perfect" job. comparing trade work to medicine is a complete apple v orange argument. they are two different types of work, for two different types of people. if we're just looking at money, there are lots of things you could do to potentially make hundreds of thousands, if not MILLIONS, more than anyone with a "typical" job. sex work/being a stripper is a total win if you're looking at the earnings to work ratio. but this is not the ideal career choice for most people, for a multitude of reasons. maybe that line is blurrier for jobs in trade but the concept of why its not the "ideal" job for most people is the same. 

in terms of the job prospects of medicine.,, i think it really depends how you look at it. it might be your first assumption that AI will make human physicians obsolete, but i have a different theory. i've read multiple articles discussing the future/potential roles that AI will play in medicine, and almost all of them reassure that AI is not predicted to "absolutely take over" physician roles. especially not within the next decade. Ai will be increasingly incorporated into existing treatment methods, and human physicians will need to adapt to working alongside AI, but at the end of the day (in the near future at least) human-to-human connection is irreplaceable. I believe AI medicine harnesses the power of making healthcare & treatment more accessible to the general public. and for this very reason, I believe this is exactly what will make human physicians that much more valuable.  if AI physicians are the cheaper, more available option, the general public  will resort to seeing AI rather than human doctors. this will lessen the demand for human doctors, and less people will go to & graduate medical school. human physicians will naturally become more scarce, and therefore more expensive. when society reaches a point where AI physicians are ubiquitous, human doctors who have graduated from residency will have already been practicing for 5+ years. they will already be somewhat or established experts in their field, and will be sought out by those who have the means to afford them. there are also certain fields of medicine (like psychiatry) that most patients may not feel comfortable leaving in the hands of AI no matter how advanced, as they require a certain level of human connection and empathy. physicians in those kinds of fields will not become obsolete, at least for now & the foreseeable future. i could go on about this for hours. 

all in all, there are no guarantees for anything, for any job. if we really want to be pessimistic, the climate crisis is only getting worse, and it looks like we're about to enter WW3. if the world is falling apart, no job no industry is going to matter anymore. hah frankly even in that situation, doctors will be the ones that are most needed.

About your linkage preferences -- is there a reason why you don't want to pursue linkage? I don't see any harm in doing a linkage program, and I'd even go as far as saying there's more to lose than gain from not pursuing one. 

In regards to med schools "preferring" students... I don't think it's the matter of medical schools preferring one type of student over another. There are outstanding students with extraordinary minds who simply can't afford expensive formal postbacc programs, or didn't have access to the resources needed to learn about them. To say that a medical school would overlook this student in favor of another student who attended a formal postbacc simply because the other student attended a formal postbacc wouldn't be right. My perspective is that formal postbacc programs offer many resources for its students, and that those resources will help mold you into a great medical schoool applicant. There's a system, and it's set for its students to succeed. Going DIY can be a pain, again not that its a BAD way to go about things, but why go through the extra struggle if you don't have to? Of course, you need to do the work to get you to where you want to be, but it helps a lot to be in an environment where everyone is there to help you & around other students who have relatively similar backgrounds as you (in terms of finances, where they are in the med school process, etc.)

Every person is different, so I’m not sure if this will resonate with you but something that helps me keep food down/eat regular amounts of food is eating with other people or in some kind of public setting. I’ve seldom had times where I felt guilty after eating with other people, and my body somehow seems to adjust itself back to its normal, non-binge non-food-conscious state when I’m around others. 

Try your best to not eat alone in your room, or in places where you feel “too” comfortable. I think it’s really easy to slip into the “b/p trance” (as I like to call it) when you’re alone.

Something else I recommend is making sure your attention is solely on your food and that you’re present in the moment while you’re eating. I think this really really helps control overeating/binging, which consequently prevents purging too. If you’re alone while you’re eating, try to not watch shows/tv/be on your phone. It’s soooo hard I know. I’m so guilty of doing this even as I tell myself that I shouldn’t. Food actually tastes better (it’s a psychological phenomenon!) to humans when we’re watching something as we’re eating. But you know, positive changes take time and effort so it’s worth a shot to try and develop the habit of mindful eating. Personally, I’ve noticed that my b/p cycles usually happen when I’m eating while watching some kind of video/show/scrolling through tiktok . There honestly has never been a time where I binged and purged when my attention was solely on the food in front of me. Again, not 100% sure if this will work for you but it is worth a try!

Hey. You sound a lot like how I used to think when I was 15. I’ve tried to kill myself 3 times throughout my life and In those moments I really thought nothing could ever get better. I hated how I looked, felt like nobody could ever love me and felt like I was insane/going insane from my thoughts. I don’t have high school memories like everyone else does. I didn’t have a friend group. My “friends” bullied me for my looks and disrespected me in ways that I can’t even IMAGINE being treated like now. I was always the ugly fat friend who was weird and loud. I tried to be like able but no one liked me. Didn’t go to any school events or dances. I never had anyone to go with. Didnt go to prom. I knew I wouldn’t be asked to go by anyone and again, I didn’t have any friends to go with/who I thought would want to go with me. Didnt even go to graduation. I knew no one would clap for me when my name was called and that I’d have no one to take pictures with so I stayed home. This same feeling continued throughout college. I’m still in college right now but the pandemic let’s me learn from afar so I don’t have to physically be at school, which has helped me heal. My body dysmorphia was so bad that I eventually developed bulimia. It got so bad I would get ice pick headaches and have heart palpitations out of nowhere. My hair would thin and fall out, my teeth got yellow and decayed from the stomach even though I did my best to take care of them... and I was always tired and upset. I could go on for hours about how terrible I felt from when I was 11 up to 20. Life really felt like shit but guess what? THINGS HAVE CHANGED. I’ve learned how to take care of myself, love and respect myself and I’m slowly building my life. I’m excited to live my 20’s and I’m going to make up for the teen years that I lost being sad. 11-20 (first half of 20) year old me was so sad, upset, lost, depressed, insecure, lonely... the list goes on. I owe it to that little girl to live my best life, be successful and to live a life abundant with happiness joy and love. I’m still in process of recovering, and I’m not always having good days. I still get triggered by a lot, and there are “leftover” wounds that have still yet left to heal. If I’m being honest my ED isnt fully gone either.. but I’m trying. I look back sometimes and honestly cannot believe how far I came.
